applicabilityBasis.summary: Tempo identifies pathUSD as a Bridge-issued, 1:1 USD-reserve-backed quote and fallback fee token that participates in payment routing. Its token-specific documentation describes minting with USDC.e and redemption to USDC. GENIUS section 2(22) additionally requires an issuer obligation to redeem for monetary value, excluding a digital asset denominated in monetary value. The opened general BBI terms provide dollar redemption for BBI-issued stablecoins but do not name pathUSD or independently establish its exact legal issuer. Payment-settlement design is supported; the token-specific statutory redemption-obligor mapping remains unresolved.

genius.notes: The opened Open Issuance announcement describes platform-level GENIUS-ready compliance and names other products, but does not make an explicit pathUSD GENIUS-pathway statement. It therefore does not support issuer-announced-intent for this token. OCC Decision 1365 concerns the separate proposed Bridge National Trust Bank, not a GENIUS grant to the current token issuer. The existing issuerEntity Bridge Building Inc., issuerDomicile, licensingRegulator, primaryFederalRegulator and domestic foreign-exception assertion are omitted because the opened token-specific source identifies Bridge only as a brand. This removes a load-bearing issuer-key attribution rather than substituting another entity. General BBI redemption terms and general Bridge quarterly reporting do not establish token-specific fiat-redemption or monthly-attestation findings, so those optional booleans are omitted. The exact path_usd public API supports reserve-disclosure presence only, not independent assurance or statutory compliance. DASP timing is the pre-effective GENIUS posture, not a legal permission to distribute the token.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of the 2026-10-07 review, no public token-specific GENIUS PPSI approval, state qualification, official GENIUS application, registered foreign exception or explicit issuer GENIUS-pathway announcement for pathUSD was located in the named sources. The identified OCC charter decision applies to a separate proposed bank. Public bank-license tables and indexed searches are not complete GENIUS registers and cannot rule out nonpublic filings. No exact legal token-issuer entity is inferred from the Bridge brand.
